metadata.title: The Variable Number of Tandem Repeats Polymorphism of the Dopamine Transporter Gene Is Not Associated with Significant Change in Dopamine Transporter Phenotype in Humans

entities.name: SLC6A3
entities.description: Gene coding for the dopamine transporter (DAT); VNTR polymorphism in its 3' untranslated region was studied.

entities.name: amphetamine-induced dopamine release
synonyms: decrease in [123I]IBZM binding potential after amphetamine
entities.description: Neurochemical phenotype measured by the decrease in [123I]IBZM binding after amphetamine challenge.

entities.name: DAT expression
entities.description: Dopamine transporter availability/expression measured by [123I]b-CIT binding.

entities.name: schizophrenia
entities.description: Diagnostic group included in the imaging study.

entities.name: healthy controls
entities.description: Control group without neurological or psychiatric illness.

relations.mechanism: The paper tested whether SLC6A3 VNTR status alters amphetamine-induced synaptic dopamine release measured by [123I]IBZM displacement.
relations.quantitative_effect: SLC6A3*9R carriers: 14.4 ± 13.8% vs SLC6A3*10R homozygotes: 10.3 ± 10.2% displacement; p = .16
relations.evidence: No significant effect of DAT VNTR status on amphetamine-induced dopamine release was found; the SLC6A3*9R carrier group showed 14.4 ± 13.8% displacement of [123I]IBZM compared to 10.3 ± 10.2% for the SLC6A3*10R homozygote group (p = .16).

relations.mechanism: The paper tested whether SLC6A3 VNTR status alters DAT availability/expression measured by [123I]b-CIT binding.
relations.quantitative_effect: SLC6A3*9R carriers: 8.1 ± 1.8 vs SLC6A3*10R homozygotes: 8.1 ± 1.4; p = .97
relations.evidence: Analysis of variance revealed no significant effect of diagnosis or VNTR status on [123I]b-CIT V3''; the mean [123I]b-CIT V3'' in the SLC6A3*9R carrier group was 8.1 ± 1.8 compared to 8.1 ± 1.4 for the SLC6A3*10R homozygote group (p = .97).

relations.mechanism: Within patients with schizophrenia, SLC6A3*9R carriers showed greater amphetamine-induced decrease in [123I]IBZM binding potential than 10R homozygotes, but the difference was not significant.
relations.evidence: The mean displacement of [123I]IBZM following amphetamine in SLC6A3*9R carrier subjects with schizophrenia was 21.0 ± 16.2% compared to 14.5 ± 11.7% in SLC6A3*10R homozygote subjects with schizophrenia (p = .24).

relations.mechanism: Within healthy controls, SLC6A3*9R carriers showed greater amphetamine-induced decrease in [123I]IBZM binding potential than 10R homozygotes, but the difference was not significant.
relations.evidence: The SLC6A3*9R carrier control subjects showed a mean displacement of 8.3 ± 7.8%, whereas SLC6A3*10R homozygote control subjects showed a mean displacement of 6.6 ± 7.2% (p = .55).
